author: nullable_carrier_review
objective: Concrete independent acceptance inputs for the next shared semantica-numeric primitive owner. No source interpreter, candidate implementation output, query AST, or SPARQL catch machinery supplies the expected answers.

independence.basis: Read pinned reference and original sources; derive exact coefficients/exponents by integer arithmetic and decimal rounding rules. Constants were authored before the future shared core is implemented. Record-writing and schema checks do not execute arithmetic implementations.
independence.prior_authorship: This reviewer authored portions of prior chain transport and tests; these new numeric expectations are independently derived from the pinned sources and mathematics, not from those bounded numeric outputs.
independence.not_claimed: No observation of the original application's active Decimal context; no parity claim for the C decimal engine's complete trapped flags; no public nullable profile qualification.

interface_contract.proposal: DecimalContext::apply(op, &a, Option<&b>, &NumericLimits) -> Result<NumericOutcome<DecimalValue>, NumericFault>; exact parse/format and exact integer operations are distinct core entry points. Names are test-adapter operations, not a demand to expose a query API.
interface_contract.decimal_value: finite{negative:bool, coefficient:nonnegative decimal digit string with no leading zeros except 0, exponent:signed base-10 integer string}; infinity{negative}; nan{negative, signaling, payload:canonical digit string or empty}. Trailing coefficient zeros are meaningful. Exponent uses a string so no JSON/i64 precision loss is assumed.
interface_contract.integer_value: {kind:integer, decimal:canonical signed base-10 string}; arbitrary precision subject to explicit resource/input limits, with no implicit Decimal rounding.
interface_contract.expected_value: Compare kind/sign/coefficient/exponent/payload exactly. Numerical equality alone is insufficient for scale and signed zero. If fixed is present, separately assert no-precision fixed formatting matches it without reparsing the value.
interface_contract.traps: For kind=trap, assert primary, result_absent and every signals_required item. signals_exact=null means complete trapped flag parity is deliberately not claimed. source_condition names the reference internal condition and is diagnostic metadata, not an extra mandatory public subtype.
interface_contract.signals: Successful/untrapped outcomes require exactly signals_exact, treated as an unordered set. Collect signals for each operation with initially clear flags; a library with sticky Context flags must clear them before each step or expose a per-operation delta.
interface_contract.inputs: Each {decimal:text} operand is independently constructed exactly, without context rounding; {integer:text} is an exact BigInt. A {ref:name} consumes the saved DecimalValue directly, never fixed-formats/reparses it. Parsing operands is not an implicit unary-plus operation.
interface_contract.sequences: Execute steps in listed order; save the actual value after a successful step and compare that intermediate value before using it. Do not reassociate or compute a rational exact end result before one final rounding.
interface_contract.context: All context fields are explicit test parameters. decimal28 models the pinned source DefaultContext only. decimal3 contexts are intentionally selected synthetic core controls, not original application observations.
interface_contract.safety_note: Limits are a proposed active safety contract. Extreme exponent cases compare compact coefficient/exponent tuples; they must not first expand 10^abs(exponent). No budget failure may masquerade as an arithmetic SPARQL/type error.

rdf_cached_numeric_boundary.fact: The original Literal constructor retains its parsed Decimal value while replacing lexical text during normalization. Positive exponent information can disappear from the real RDF lexical string. A global numeric cache keyed only by RDF term identity cannot restore per-object construction metadata.

remaining_unknowns: Actual historical application Decimal context may differ from mutable DefaultContext; transitive initialization and active-context observation were not executed.
The C _decimal engine may collect more flags before a trapped exception than this pure-Python reference; exact complete trapped flag sets remain unqualified.
C Decimal constructor hard exponent/payload domain limits and Python integer text-limit configuration are not inferred from arbitrary-size internal BigInt representation.

Binary64/float-to-Decimal exact conversion, FloatOperation flags, float/decimal mixing and RDFLib binary64 xsd:float differences require their own cases; FloatOperation is reserved in the signal model but not falsely covered here.
Rounding modes other than HALF_EVEN, quantize, remainder/divide-integer, power, square root and transcendental operations are outside this core case set.

RDF datatype promotion, derived integer validity/normalization, invalid numeric RDF lexicals, RDF EBV/comparison and private per-cell cached metadata are adapter work; successful core tests do not complete them.

RDFLib catches InvalidOperation/ZeroDivisionError around multiplicative expressions, while additive/unary catch boundaries differ. This belongs to the existing expression compiler/adapter, not the numeric core.
No legacy normalizer corpus, public all-targets build, /1-4 regression, native behavior or public /5 qualification is claimed by this record.

acceptance_gate.required: A Rust test adapter must run all 70 cases against the one shared numeric core, checking every intermediate tuple and signal assertion. Active safety cases are reported separately from parity/source-derived cases. Candidate implementation must not regenerate these expectations.

acceptance_gate.completeness_limit: Passing this set proves this explicit finite primitive surface under its stated contexts and budgets. It does not prove every Decimal operation/input domain or RDFLib query equivalence.
